messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx and connection errors observed from services routing through us-east-1 (ALB/ELB control plane + Route53 resolution anomalies). Auto-page oncall at 2026-03-15T02:12:30Z.

Aisha Patel: acknowledged. suppressing duplicate alerts and taking initial triage. whos on for handoff?

Sam Chen: Ill join, seeing multiple ALB target groups with health check flapping in us-east-1, and a surge of 502/504s in front-door logs.

Jorge Martinez: cross-checking AWS status and our watchers. AWS reports partial ELB control-plane errors in us-east-1 and some Route53 resolver latencies affecting a small set of POPs. internal watcher: https://internal.redwood/monitoring/events/1749999999

incident-bot: sys: created incident channel #incidents/INC-2026-03-15-us-east-networking

Aisha Patel: ops summary for incident record: public API endpoints returning 5xx for ~25-35% of traffic over last 15m, higher failure rate for long-sequence generation. Several Dedicated customers with region pinning reporting throughput drops due to instance deregistration/attach retries and EBS detach delays.

Maya Kim: CS: notified affected customers at 02:25Z, promise updates every 15m. escalation open for 1 enterprise customer.

Jorge Martinez: preliminary cause hypothesis: ELB control plane degraded causing slower target state transitions; concurrently some AZ-to-edge routing flaps mean Route53 caches keep returning unhealthy POPs until TTLs expire.

Priya Rao: suggested mitigations:
- immediate: lower relevant DNS TTLs to 30s and introduce weighted routing to divert traffic to us-west-2
- immediate: shorten ALB health checks to fail faster and reduce deregistration delay to speed draining of bad targets
- medium: spin up warmed inference nodes in us-west-2, attach EBS from snapshots if needed
- medium: enable cross-region fallback for Dedicated customers and throttle large-seq work to reduce resource pressure

Sam Chen: applying DNS changes now (commands shown):
```
# set low TTL weighted records
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZHJ12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","TTL":30,"WeightedRoutingPolicy":{"Weight":20},"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"52.23.45.66"}]}}]}'
```

Sam Chen: created weighted entries with initial 80/20 (us-east/us-west) and reducing to 60/40 while we confirm. monitoring edge POP latencies.

Aisha Patel: go for TTL change + weight tilt. Priya, can you prep AMIs in us-west-2 and a small pool to register? Jorge, check Dedicated pool reservations in us-west-2.

Jorge Martinez: checking capacity — reserved + on-demand headroom OK in us-west-2. EBS gp3 quotas sufficient. will prepare a few volumes from latest snapshots.

Priya Rao: AMIs and startup script pushed to us-west-2 region. launching 8 instances and preloading model cache.

Sam Chen: adjusted ALB healthcheck interval to 8s and unhealthy threshold=2, set deregistration_delay=120s for graceful drain. initiating traffic shift to 55/45 now.

incident-bot: aws-status-bot: AWS update: ELB control plane in us-east-1 experiencing elevated errors; Route53 service showing increased resolver latencies in select edge locations.

Maya Kim: CS update sent 02:45Z: "Were seeing an AWS networking disruption impacting us-east-1. Were diverting traffic to us-west-2 and expect progressive recovery. Will update again in 30m." :email:

Sam Chen: after initial weight shift, 5xx rate dropped from ~33% -> ~14%. latency for requests routed to us-west-2 increased by ~35-50ms but success rate improved.

Aisha Patel: handing off primary oncall to Sam for the next watch window. Ill move to secondary and stay available for escalation.

Sam Chen: handoff accepted. runbook pointers: watch ALB 5xx, Route53 resolver latency, EBS attach/detach error logs. CS cadence every 30m.

Jorge Martinez: note: VPC flow logs show increased retransmits between us-east-1 AZ-b and a subset of POPs; AWS NOC ticket opened. this probably explains the health-check flapping.

Sam Chen: considering draining the AZ-b node pool to prevent EBS thundering and reduce attach retries; plan to drain one AZ at a time with 2m connection drain.

Priya Rao: initiating drain for us-east-1b targets and shifting their load out. AMI-backed instances in us-west-2 are online and registered in target groups.

Sam Chen: executing deregistration:
```
ALB: deregister targets tg-0abcde in us-east-1b, deregistration delay 120s
ALB: register targets tg-9fghij in us-west-2
```

incident-bot: sys: updated INC-2026-03-15-us-east-networking: DNS TTL lowered, weighted DNS applied, ALB healthchecks tuned, cross-region fallback enabled for affected Dedicated groups.

Maya Kim: CS update 03:30Z: "Most customers report successful requests. A small subset with strict geo-pinning may still see degraded throughput; support is coordinating manual reroutes." :thumbsup:

Sam Chen: current metrics: 5xx ~4% and trending downward. keeping watch for two more cycles (approx 60-90m) before reversing weight.

Jorge Martinez: AWS status showing partial recovery of ELB control plane. recommend keep low TTL for 2 hours and perform gradual weight normalization only after 30m of stability. collecting ELB debug logs, CloudWatch traces, and VPC flow logs for RCA.

Aisha Patel: thanks. Ill write a short incident summary and follow up with a full post-incident report in ~2h. tagging RCA lead @Jorge Martinez.

Jorge Martinez: will take RCA. preliminary root cause: simultaneous ELB control-plane degradation in us-east-1 plus regional routing flaps to certain POPs that extended unhealthy state durations and caused EBS attach/deregister retries.

Sam Chen: staying on until 04:10Z for final checks. ping me for urgent escalations.

incident-bot: INC-2026-03-15-us-east-networking: Mitigations applied, impact reduced, monitoring continues. :white_check_mark:
